chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no pre-payment (sabaq) except in a camel's hoof, or a horse's hoof, or an arrowhead, meaning archery.

key_terms.النِّضَالَ: Archery / The act of shooting arrows
key_terms.سَبَق: Pre-payment or prize money in a race

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible forms of racing for pre-payment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the permissible scope of 'sabaq' (prize money in competitions) to three specific domains: camel racing, horse racing, and archery, which were central to military preparedness in early Islamic society. By restricting wagers to these activities, the Imams emphasized the martial and practical utility of the skills being tested, distinguishing them from mere entertainment. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking legal permissibility to the preservation of strength and readiness for defense.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umey, from Hafs, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There shall be no (coming) first except in (racing) a camel-hoof, or a horse hoof, or an arrow-head, meaning archery’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn ‘Isma’il in a marfu’ manner the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You should learn horse riding and sharp-shooting. I like your learning sharp-shooting more than your horse riding.’

He then said, ‘All playing of believers’ is falsehood except three things: horse training, sharp-shooting from his bow and playing with his wife because they are right. However, Allah, the most Majestic, the most Glorious, with the arrow sends three to paradise: one who makes the arrow, one who provides support with it for the cause of Allah and one who shoots it for the cause of Allah.’”
